answer: Locked capital per identity doubles with every head an operator adds. The jetty is a registry where identities sharing a funder, host or code fingerprint moor at one berth. A beacon, one claimed identity, is admitted only after locking a cipher, an escrowed collateral note that is refunded on clean exit and slashed if that beacon is proven a duplicate. The k-th beacon at a berth must lock a cipher worth 10 × 2^(k−1) credits, so one honest agent ties up 10 credits while 20 clones tie up about 10.5 million. It fails if clones dodge clustering at the jetty or borrowed capital is nearly free.
